questions.q: What will happen to Jerusalem’s possessions on the day that is coming for Yahweh?
questions.a: Jerusalem’s plunder will be divided up within the city.

questions.q: Why will Jerusalem’s plunder be divided in their midst?
questions.a: Jerusalem’s plunder will be divided in their midst because Yahweh will gather every nation against Jerusalem for battle, and the city will be captured. The houses will be plundered.

questions.q: What will happen to the nations that fought against Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh will go out and wage war against those nations as when he wages war on a day of battle.

questions.q: What will happen to the Mount of Olives when Yahweh stands on it?
questions.a: The Mount of Olives will be split in half, forming a very great valley between the two halves.

questions.q: When will Yahweh and the holy ones come?
questions.a: Yahweh and the holy ones will come after the inhabitants of Jerusalem flee down the valley between Yahweh’s mountains.

questions.q: What will happen to the light on that day?
questions.a: There will not be light; the bright lights will grow dim.

questions.q: What will be different about that day?
questions.a: That day will not follow the normal cycle of day and night, and even in the evening there will be light.

questions.q: Where will the running water go that flows from Jerusalem?
questions.a: Half of the water will go to the eastern sea, and half will flow toward the western sea.

questions.q: Who will be king over all the earth?
questions.a: Yahweh will be king over all the earth.

questions.q: What will happen to the land from Geba to Rimmon?
questions.a: It will become flat like a plain, but Jerusalem will rise up and remain in its place.

questions.q: What will happen to Jerusalem?
questions.a: There will not be destruction again, and Jerusalem will dwell in security.

questions.q: With what plague will Yahweh attack all the peoples that waged war against Jerusalem?
questions.a: The flesh, eyes, and tongues of all the people that waged war against Jerusalem will rot.

questions.q: What will happen when that great panic from Yahweh comes among them?
questions.a: Each man will seize his neighbor’s hand; each hand will be raised against its neighbor’s hand.

questions.q: What will Judah do at Jerusalem?
questions.a: Judah will fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of the surrounding nations will be gathered—gold, silver, and garments in great abundance.

questions.q: What will happen to the animals in the enemies’ camps?
questions.a: The horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the other animals in the camps will be struck with the same plague.

questions.q: What will all who remain in those nations that came against Jerusalem do?
questions.a: All those who remain in those nations will go up from year to year to worship the King, Yahweh of Armies, and to celebrate the Festival of Booths.

questions.q: What will happen if anyone from all the nations of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, Yahweh of Armies?
questions.a: If anyone does not go up to Jerusalem, Yahweh will not bring rain on them. A plague from Yahweh will attack the nations that do not go up to keep the Festival of Booths.

questions.q: What will be the sin of Egypt and the other nations?
questions.a: Their sin will be that they do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.

questions.q: What will be written on the bells of the horses?
questions.a: The bells of the horses will be inscribed with words saying that they are holy to Yahweh.

questions.q: On that day, who will no longer be in the house of Yahweh of Armies?
questions.a: On that day traders will no longer be selling goods in the house of Yahweh of Armies.

commentary.text: Encouraging prospects, and the destruction of her enemies.
The holiness of the latter days.

Verses 1–7 The Lord Jesus often stood upon the Mount of Olives when on earth. He ascended from thence to heaven, and then desolations and distresses came upon the Jewish nation. Such is the view taken of this figuratively; but many consider it as a notice of events yet unfulfilled, and that it relates to troubles of which we cannot now form a full idea. Every believer, being related to God as his God, may triumph in the expectation of Christ's coming in power, and speak of it with pleasure. During a long season, the state of the church would be deformed by sin; there would be a mixture of truth and error, of happiness and misery. Such is the experience of God's people, a mingled state of grace and corruption. But, when the season is at the worst, and most unpromising, the Lord will turn darkness into light; deliverance comes when God's people have done looking for it.

Some consider that the progress of the gospel, beginning from Jerusalem, is referred to by the living waters flowing from that city. Neither shall the gospel and means of grace, nor the graces of the Spirit wrought in the hearts of believers by those means, ever fail, by reason either of the heat of persecution, or storms of temptation, or the blasts of any other affliction. Tremendous judgments appear to be foretold, to be sent upon those who should oppose the settlement of the Jews in their own land. How far they are to be understood literally, events alone can determine. The furious rage and malice which stir up men against each other, are faint shadows of the enmity which reigns among those who have perished in their sins. Even the inferior creatures often suffer for the sin of man, and in his plagues. Thus God will show his displeasure against sin.

As it is impossible for all nations literally to come to Jerusalem once a year, to keep a feast, it is evident that a figurative meaning must here be applied. Gospel worship is represented by the keeping of the feast of tabernacles. Every day of a Christian's life is a day of the feast of tabernacles; every Lord's day especially is the great day of the feast; therefore every day let us worship the Lord of hosts, and keep every Lord's day with peculiar solemnity. It is just for God to withhold the blessings of grace from those who do not attend the means of grace. It is a sin that is its own punishment; those who forsake the duty, forfeit the privilege of communion with God. A time of complete peace and purity of the church will arrive. Men will carry on their common affairs, and their sacred services, upon the same holy principles of faith, love and obedience. Real holiness shall be more diffused, because there shall be a more plentiful pouring forth of the Spirit of holiness than ever before. There shall be holiness even in common things. Every action and every enjoyment of the believer, should be so regulated according to the will of God, that it may be directed to his glory. Our whole lives should be as one constant sacrifice, or act of devotion; no selfish motive should prevail in any of our actions. But how far is the Christian church from this state of purity! Other times, however, are at hand, and the Lord will reform and enlarge his church, as he has promised. Yet in heaven alone will perfect holiness and happiness be found.
